raj_customer: hey team — exporting daily usage for our org (EU/Berlin) and the CSV is cutting days at 22:00 local time, which is weird. charts in console also show day boundaries shifted by -2h. any idea?

sophia_support: sorry about that, @raj_customer — can you share the export you downloaded and the org timezone setting? quick question: is your account org-tz set to Europe/Berlin in Settings -> Billing? :thinking:

raj_customer: yes org tz = Europe/Berlin. i attached a small sample: first row has timestamp 2026-03-16T22:00:00+01:00 and it's being treated as next-day in the UI. CSV snippet below. i can DM full file.

raj_customer: ```
date,project,usage_tokens
2026-03-16T21:59:59+01:00,acme-app,450
2026-03-16T22:00:00+01:00,acme-app,30
2026-03-17T00:05:00+01:00,acme-app,120
```

liam_obs: thanks, repro looks clear. i pulled the daily-aggregation job logs for that timeframe — the aggregator used `day_cutoff = 22:00` for that org id 4693 on 2026-03-16. i see a config mismatch: exporter pipeline reads `account.timezone` but the dashboard aggregator reads `tenant.billing_tz` fallback which in some orgs is set to UTC offset.

liam_obs: probable root cause: when DST flips we have two code paths — one uses tz name (Europe/Berlin) and another uses fixed offset (+01:00). fixed-offset path incorrectly computes start_of_day in utc and then converts, resulting in 2h shift.

maria_eng: digging into code now. i can see the code in services/usage/rollup.go: we call `StartOfDay(t, tz)` but if tz is serialized as offset we end up doing `StartOfDayUTC` incorrectly. quick fix is to canonicalize timezone to IANA name at ingestion time and failover to UTC only if unknown. adding unit test for DST day and non-DST day. @liam_obs can you paste the job id from logs?

liam_obs: job id `rollup-20260316-4693` — attached logs show `tz_serialized: +01:00`. also saw one related warning: `WARN: fallback_tz_serialized` right before batch commit.

maria_eng: ok i'll push a patch to normalize tz values and a migration to recompute rollups for the affected date range. initial patch will go to canary, then to prod. work estimate: patch + tests 2-3hrs, canary deploy + 1hr, backfill run depends on range (~3-4hrs for 30 days).

sophia_support: @raj_customer sorry for the disruption — short-term workaround: when exporting use the API with explicit `tz=Europe/Berlin` query param (we'll accept tz in IANA format) and the CSV will align with your expectation. we'll also add a UI label to note timezone discrepancies until fix lands.

raj_customer: thanks — i'll try the API param, appreciate the proposed fix and ETA. will you notify when backfill is complete? :pray:

maria_eng: yes — i'll post updates here. plan: patch to main -> canary deploy at 1966003500 -> validate for 1 hour -> prod deploy. if canary looks good we'll run backfill for 2026-03-01..2026-03-31 first.

deploy-bot: deploy started: canary rollout for service usage-rollup (revision: f2b9c3a) at 1966003500.

deploy-bot: canary health: 2/2 pods healthy. no errors in canary window.

maria_eng: canary passed. scheduling prod deploy and backfill. i'll follow up with PR link and backfill job id.

sophia_support: closing loop: added temporary support note in ticket #8472 with API export workaround. will ping once backfill done and UI label added.

raj_customer: perfect, thanks everyone. much appreciated. :thumbsup:
